intent: Increased sensor size to 0.016 m to improve line coverage and reduce noise sensitivity, widened wheel track to 0.16 m to enhance stability and reduce steering oscillation, and reduced mass to 0.7 kg to improve acceleration and progress. Expect fewer line loss events, smoother steering, and better completion rates, especially on challenging tracks like the slalom.
rationale: The integration feedback and race data indicate that the current symmetric 5-sensor array with 0.012 m sensor size provides good line detection and steering precision, but there is room to reduce line loss events and improve stability. Increasing the sensor size to 0.016 m should enhance coverage and reduce noise sensitivity, potentially lowering line loss events, especially on challenging tracks like the slalom. Widening the wheel track from 0.14 m to 0.16 m is expected to improve stability and reduce steering oscillation, as suggested by the integrator's experience. Reducing the mass from 0.8 kg to 0.7 kg should improve acceleration and progress, helping the robot complete more trials and finish faster. The sensor positions remain symmetric and evenly spaced to maintain balanced line detection. Wheel radius, body width, and body length are kept unchanged to isolate the effects of these changes. The expected result is improved line tracking, fewer line loss events, reduced steering oscillation, and better overall progress and completion rates, especially on the more difficult tracks.
